title: Launch Radar: Consolidated Signal Calendar and Fail-Forward Escalation Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: create a single-source "Launch Radar" that consolidates cross-surface launch signals (runtime, console, API) into a predictable calendar and a fail-forward escalation playbook. Deliverables: (1) canonical signal taxonomy and visibility lanes (green/yellow/red) for latency, error-rate, capacity, and quality regressions; (2) a syncable calendar view that maps lanes to regional cutover windows and blackout constraints; (3) automated guardrail rules (backpressure, capacity hedging) and on-call escalation flows; (4) a preflight checklist and automated gating hook for CI/CD and release orchestration.
updates:
2025-02-12: Kickoff — scope agreed with runtime and console leads. Decided to focus first on regional cutovers for EU/NA before APAC.
2025-02-14: Draft taxonomy shared; Silva (Eng) suggested separating model-quality signals from infra signals to avoid noisy false positives.
2025-02-16: PM/Design sync — Priya to prototype calendar UI with traffic lanes; flagged need for a lightweight API for signal ingestion.
2025-02-18: Engineering feasibility review — Marcelo and Lena confirmed automated backpressure can be implemented as policy rules in the router, but requires ENG-30503 for routing API.
2025-02-20: Updated scope — add explicit rollback and fail-forward criteria to playbook; added telemetry dashboards to acceptance criteria. Next: finalize PRD and assign ENG spikes for signal ingestion and calendar API.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical signal taxonomy documented and agreed by runtime/console/SDK teams
Calendar UI prototype with per-region lanes and blackout windows that can be exported to calendar feeds
Automated guardrail rules implemented as policy templates (backpressure, capacity hedge, model-fallback) and validated in a staging canary
Escalation playbook with owners, SLAs, and fail-forward actions published in Confluence
Telemetry dashboard showing signal-to-action mapping and post-launch postmortem metrics (latency, errors, capacity, quality)
impact_summary: Launch Radar reduces cross-team ambiguity during coordinated launches by centralizing signals and automating first-line remediation. Expected benefits: 30-50% faster mitigation for launch-related incidents, clearer owner handoffs, fewer manual aborts during regional cutovers, and measurable reduction in token-cost spikes from runaway workloads. This feeds directly into runtime SLO stability and improves time-to-value for dedicated/private customers.
